claims.text: Grain size governs the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys.
Phase distribution governs the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of these alloys.
Applied magnetic field interacts with microstructure in governing the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis.
Annealing treatments can be used to produce controlled variation in grain size.
Changes in magnetic-domain structure affect the magnetocaloric response.
Smaller grain sizes may reduce hysteresis losses.
Decreasing grain size will reduce hysteresis losses relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Decreasing grain size will improve the magnetocaloric response relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The predictions are proposed to hold for grain sizes from 10 nm to 10 μm.
The predictions are proposed to hold at applied magnetic fields up to 2 T.
The exact relationship among grain size, phase distribution, and magnetocaloric response is not well established.
The optimal grain size for minimizing hysteresis losses is unknown.
A lack of significant correlation between grain size and hysteresis loss would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies annealing to vary grain size, but the prediction requires decreasing grain size relative to an as-deposited baseline. No annealing parameters or processing route is given to show that annealing will refine rather than grow the as-deposited grains.
